headlines: CLOSE THE APP. OPEN A DEAL.

Action beats motivation. Open Marketplace and move.
Broke is a habit. So is hustle. Choose your habit.
The buyer is online right now. Be there first.
You don't need more time. You need fewer distractions.
Every "later" is a sale you didn't make.
Discipline today. Freedom tomorrow.
Stop feeding the feed. Feed your bank account.
Winners list. Everyone else scrolls.

Small sales stack. Stack one today.

Less feed. More deals.
tips: Use daylight and a plain background for photos. Clean photos sell faster than fancy ones.
Check sold listings for similar items before you price. Price just under what buyers actually paid.
Write a clear title with the brand, size, model and condition. Buyers search for those words.
Describe every flaw. Honest listings get fewer time-wasting messages and fewer returns.
Reply to buyers quickly. Listings with fast replies sell faster.
Relist an item that has no interest after a few days, with a new photo or a lower price.
Bundle small items together to get a better total price and clear your space faster.
Meet in a public place in daylight, or use a safe handoff spot, and bring a friend if you can.
Never share verification codes, passwords or payment links from strangers. A real buyer does not need them.
Set a minimum price you will accept before you start negotiating, and stick to it.
Ask for cash or a secure payment method on pickup, and check it before you hand over the item.
Measure furniture and clothing and put the numbers in the listing. Fewer questions means faster sales.
Sell things you no longer use first. Clearing a shelf can fund your next move.
Take the photo of the item in use or on a hanger. It helps buyers picture it.
Post in the local categories that match the item. The right category gets more eyes on it.
Set a daily Marketplace routine: list one item, reply to every message, and close one deal.
Price for a quick sale first. You can always raise a price later, but you cannot undo a slow month.
Keep a simple spreadsheet of what you listed, what it sold for and how long it took. Use it to get better.
Use the same clear format for every listing so you can work faster.
Ignore lowball offers that insult the item. A polite counter-offer usually closes the deal.
Turn on notifications for Marketplace messages, so no buyer waits hours for an answer.
Bring the item's original box, manual or accessories. They add value and build trust.
Check the item works before you list it, and say so in the listing.
Ask a buyer to confirm the pickup time the day before. Confirmed sales are less likely to fall through.
Sell in a local area where you can meet easily. Shipping cuts into the profit on small items.
Look for things you can clean and resell, like tools, bikes, kids' gear and kitchenware.
If you are not sure about an item's value, search for the exact model number before you post.
Keep a folder of your best listing photos and descriptions so new listings take minutes, not an hour.
Close the loop. When a sale is done, mark it sold so buyers don't waste your time.
Track your hours. If an item takes more time than it earns, stop listing that type of item.
Keep a small profit goal for each week. Smaller goals are easier to hit and keep you going.
Learn the Marketplace fees and rules for your area before you start, so you keep more of each sale.
